function.name: %tool.findTools.name
function.shortDescription: Finds more tools by English keywords or area when none of yours fits. Returns ids and one-line descriptions; the tools are yours from the next step.
function.description: Finds agent tools you were not given by English keywords and/or an area, and returns their ids, area, class and one-line description. Call it when none of your tools fits the task (for example backups, jobs, grants, DDL, data export, deadlocks, index fragmentation). The tools it returns are offered from your next step on; then call them by id. If nothing matches it lists the areas and their tool ids.

parameter.name: query
parameter.description: English keywords, for example: backup history, kill session, foreign keys

parameter.name: connection
parameter.description: Connection id or name; only tools that work on it

function.name: %tool.listConnections.name
function.shortDescription: Lists the connections: id, name, driver, production, readOnly. Use when no connection is set or the user names one.
function.description: Lists the connections configured in Chromite: id, name, folder, driver, family, connection type, production, readOnly, color, connected. Use it when no connection is set or the user names one; pass the id or name as the 'connection' argument of other tools. For one connection's host, user and versions use getConnectionInfo.

parameter.name: filter
parameter.description: Optional text to match in name, driver or folder
parameter.shortDescription: Text in name, driver or folder

function.name: %tool.getConnectionInfo.name
function.description: Settings of one connection without secrets: host, port, database, user, auth model, network handlers (SSH, proxy), default auto-commit, and server product, server version and driver version when connected. Does not connect. For edition, uptime and server settings use getServerInfo; to open the connection use connect.

parameter.name: connection
parameter.description: Connection id or name (listConnections); default: the chat's current connection

function.name: %tool.connect.name
function.description: Opens the connection if it is closed and returns the getConnectionInfo details plus connectMs. Rarely needed: every tool connects on demand. To check whether a connection works use testConnection.

function.name: %tool.disconnect.name
function.description: Closes the connection for the whole Chromite app, query windows included. Only when the user asks to disconnect; uncommitted transactions make the user choose commit, roll back or cancel first. To stop the agent's running statement use cancelQuery; to end another server session use killSession.

function.name: %tool.testConnection.name
function.description: Checks that a connection works: connects, makes one round trip and returns ok, roundTripMs and the server product and version. Use when the user asks whether a connection works or is slow to reach. For connection settings use getConnectionInfo.

function.name: %tool.getCurrentDatabase.name
function.description: Current database and schema of the agent's session (agentDatabase, agentSchema) and of the connection's main session (connectionDatabase, connectionSchema). To list databases use listDatabases; to change the agent's default use setCurrentDatabase.

function.name: %tool.setCurrentDatabase.name
function.description: Changes the database and/or schema that the agent's later calls on this connection use (the user's query windows do not change) and returns the getCurrentDatabase result. For one call only, pass that tool's 'database' argument instead.

parameter.name: database
parameter.description: Database (catalog) name; empty for the connection default

function.name: %tool.getServerInfo.name
function.description: Server product, version, edition, uptime, host facts and key settings. Call it first on a connection before diagnosing: the version decides which system views and tools work. For connection settings (host, user) use getConnectionInfo; for setting checks use getServerConfig. SQL Server, PostgreSQL, MySQL/MariaDB, Oracle.

function.name: %tool.probePermissions.name
function.description: What this login may read for diagnosis: system views, server permissions and extensions (VIEW SERVER STATE, pg_monitor, PROCESS, V$ access, pg_stat_statements, ...) and which tools are limited without them. Call it before a health check or after a diagnostic tool fails on permissions. Not for database users and grants (listPrincipals, listPermissions) nor Chromite's tool permissions (getToolPolicy). SQL Server, PostgreSQL, MySQL/MariaDB, Oracle.

function.name: %tool.getTransactionStatus.name
function.shortDescription: Whether the agent or the user's query windows have an open transaction on the connection.
function.description: Whether the agent has an open transaction on the connection (uncommitted changes, locks or a snapshot, or one begun explicitly, also in auto-commit mode), and whether the user's query windows have one or one that could not be checked. Use before commit, rollback or disconnect. For old transactions of all server sessions use listOpenTransactions.

function.name: %tool.commitTransaction.name
function.shortDescription: Commits the agent's open transaction. Only when the user asked to keep the changes.
function.description: Commits the agent's open transaction on the connection (left open by runSql, runScript or a data tool). Call it only when the user asked to keep the changes; the user still chooses commit, roll back or cancel. Never touches the user's query windows.

function.name: %tool.rollbackTransaction.name
function.shortDescription: Rolls back the agent's open transaction.
function.description: Rolls back the agent's open transaction on the connection, discarding the agent's uncommitted changes. The user confirms. Never touches the user's query windows.

function.name: %tool.getToolPolicy.name
function.description: Chromite's permission for every agent tool on a connection: AUTO (runs), CONFIRM (asks the user), BLOCKED or READ_ONLY, with the reason, plus the production and read-only flags. Plan around blocked tools instead of calling them. Not the database's own permissions: use listPermissions or probePermissions.

parameter.name: connection
parameter.description: Connection id or name (empty: rules without a connection)

function.name: %tool.listDatabases.name
function.description: Names of the databases (catalogs) on the server and the current one. For their sizes use getDatabaseSizes; for the schemas of a database use listSchemas.

function.name: %tool.listSchemas.name
function.description: Schemas of a database and the current schema. MySQL/MariaDB have no schemas inside a database: use listDatabases there. For the tables of a schema use listTables.

function.name: %tool.listTables.name
function.shortDescription: Tables and views of one schema with type and comment.
function.description: Tables and views of one schema (MySQL/MariaDB: one database) with type and comment, count and hasMore. Use to browse a schema. To find an object by name in any schema use searchObjects; for columns use describeTable; for row counts and sizes use getTableStatistics.

function.name: %tool.describeTable.name
function.shortDescription: Columns, primary key, indexes and foreign keys of one table or view.
function.description: Full structure of one table or view: columns (type, size, nullable, default, auto-increment, comment), primary key, indexes, foreign keys and the foreign keys of other tables that reference it. Use it first for any question about a table's structure; listIndexes and listForeignKeys return parts of it. For the CREATE statement use getObjectDdl.

parameter.name: table
parameter.description: Table or view: name, schema.name or database.schema.name

function.name: %tool.listIndexes.name
function.description: Only the index definitions of one table: name, unique, ordered key columns, filter (describeTable includes them too). For how indexes are used use getIndexUsage; for unused or duplicate ones getUnusedIndexes; for suggested new ones getMissingIndexes.

function.name: %tool.listForeignKeys.name
function.description: Only the foreign keys of one table: outgoing (it references others) and incoming (others reference it), with columns and ON DELETE/UPDATE rules (describeTable includes them too). For dependencies through views, routines and triggers use getObjectDependencies.

function.name: %tool.listRoutines.name
function.description: Procedures and functions of a schema (MySQL/MariaDB: database): schema, name, type, comment. For a routine's code use getRoutineSource; for its run-time statistics getRoutineStats; for triggers listTriggers.

function.name: %tool.getRoutineSource.name
function.description: Source of one procedure, function, trigger or view with LINE NUMBERS (cite them), plus parameters and properties. Use to review or explain logic. For the generated CREATE DDL of a table or other object use getObjectDdl. SQL Server, PostgreSQL, MySQL/MariaDB, Oracle.

parameter.name: name
parameter.description: Routine, trigger or view: name or schema.name

function.name: %tool.listTriggers.name
function.description: Triggers of one table or of a schema: timing, events, enabled. For a trigger's code use getRoutineSource. SQL Server, PostgreSQL, MySQL/MariaDB, Oracle.

function.name: %tool.listSequences.name
function.description: Sequences with current value, increment and limits. SQL Server, PostgreSQL, MariaDB, Oracle (MySQL has none: its AUTO_INCREMENT columns show in describeTable).

function.name: %tool.listPrincipals.name
function.description: Database security principals: logins, users, roles and role memberships. Use for who has access and which roles someone has. For grants on an object or of a user use listPermissions; for what the agent's own login may read use probePermissions. SQL Server, PostgreSQL, MySQL/MariaDB, Oracle.

function.name: %tool.listPermissions.name
function.description: Granted and denied permissions on an object or schema, or of a user or role (give object, principal or both). For logins, users and role memberships use listPrincipals; for the agent's own login probePermissions; for Chromite's tool permissions getToolPolicy. SQL Server, PostgreSQL, MySQL/MariaDB, Oracle.

parameter.name: object
parameter.description: Object (table, view, routine) or schema; give this, principal, or both

parameter.name: principal
parameter.description: User or role name; give this, object, or both

function.name: %tool.getObjectDdl.name
function.description: CREATE DDL of an existing table, view, routine or other object as Chromite generates it for the database. Use to show an object's definition. To build the DDL of a change use generateDdl; for routine code with line numbers use getRoutineSource.

function.name: %tool.getObjectDependencies.name
function.description: Dependency graph of one object as nodes and edges: what it uses (tables, views, routines, foreign keys) and what uses it (views, routines, triggers); depth follows 'uses' edges. Use for impact analysis before changing or dropping an object. SQL Server, PostgreSQL, MySQL/MariaDB, Oracle.

function.name: %tool.searchObjects.name
function.shortDescription: Finds tables, views, routines and columns whose name contains a text, in all schemas.
function.description: Finds tables, views, routines (and columns when types includes column) whose name contains a text, in all schemas of one database. Use when the user names an object without its schema, or asks which table has a column. To list one schema use listTables.

parameter.name: types
parameter.description: Comma-separated: table, view, routine, column (default: tables, views, routines)

function.name: %tool.runSelect.name
function.description: Runs one read-only SELECT you write and returns one page of rows (columns, rows, hasMore, nextOffset); page on with offset. Use to read data with joins, filters or aggregates. Statements not provably read-only are refused (use runSql). For system views, SHOW, DBCC or several result sets use runReadOnlySql; for a table's rows without SQL use sampleRows.

parameter.name: offset
parameter.description: Rows to skip (default 0); use nextOffset of the previous page

parameter.name: format
parameter.description: objects (default) or arrays (columns + row arrays, smaller)

function.name: %tool.runReadOnlySql.name
function.shortDescription: Runs one read-only statement you write (SELECT, system views, SHOW) and returns its result sets. Refuses statements that may write.
function.description: Runs one read-only diagnostic statement you write (system views, SHOW, read-only DBCC, sp_who/sp_help* procedures) in a rolled-back read-only transaction; returns every result set, update counts and server messages. Use when no specific diagnostic tool covers the question. Not for paging table data (runSelect). Statements not provably read-only are refused (use runSql).

function.name: %tool.runSql.name
function.shortDescription: Runs one statement that changes data or schema. The user confirms it. On manual-commit connections the transaction stays open.
function.description: Runs one statement that may change data or schema (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, MERGE, DDL, EXEC). WRITE: the user sees the SQL and confirms unless their policy allows it; DROP, TRUNCATE and DELETE/UPDATE without WHERE are DANGEROUS. Returns results or update counts and transactionOpen; on manual-commit connections the transaction stays open until commitTransaction or rollbackTransaction. For several statements use runScript; for reads use runSelect.

parameter.name: sql
parameter.description: One statement; several statements go to runScript

parameter.name: limit
parameter.description: Rows returned if it produces results (default 100)

function.name: %tool.runScript.name
function.description: Runs a script of several statements split by the database's delimiter rules (GO for SQL Server); returns each statement's result or error. Same confirmation and transaction rules as runSql. Use for a routine rewrite or a multi-statement change; for one statement use runSql.

parameter.name: stopOnError
parameter.description: Stop at the first error (default true)

function.name: %tool.cancelQuery.name
function.description: Cancels the statements the agent itself is running on the connection; returns canceled. Not for other sessions: use killSession.

function.name: %tool.explainQuery.name
function.shortDescription: Estimated execution plan of a statement without running it, with hotspots and findings.
function.description: Estimated execution plan without running the statement, as JSON: operator tree (op, object, estRows, cost, predicates), hotspots and findings (scans, key lookups, implicit conversions, missing statistics or indexes, compiled parameter values). Start here when tuning a query. For measured rows and time use getActualPlan; to compare a rewrite comparePlans; for the plan the server cached getCachedPlans. SQL Server, PostgreSQL, MySQL/MariaDB, Oracle; others via the driver planner.

function.name: %tool.getActualPlan.name
function.description: Runs the statement and returns the actual plan with run-time values (actual rows, executions, time, reads/buffers, spills; SQL Server also STATISTICS IO/TIME messages). Use after explainQuery when estimates look wrong or measured cost is needed. Read-only statements run read-only; others become WRITE, the user confirms and they are rolled back. Oracle needs SELECT_CATALOG_ROLE. SQL Server, PostgreSQL, MySQL/MariaDB, Oracle.

function.name: %tool.comparePlans.name
function.description: Plans of two statements (a query and its rewrite) side by side with a diff: cost change and operators only in A or B; actual=true also runs both (read-only statements only) for measured time. Use to show that a rewrite is better. For a hypothetical index on PostgreSQL use whatIfIndex; to compare result rows use compareQueryResults.

parameter.name: actual
parameter.description: Run both for actual plans (default false)

function.name: %tool.validateSql.name
function.description: Checks one statement without running it: parse errors, statement type, readOnly and the access class the agent applies, plus a server check of syntax and names (SQL Server SET NOEXEC; PostgreSQL/MySQL EXPLAIN for SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE). Use before proposing or running SQL you wrote. Not a plan: use explainQuery.

parameter.name: server
parameter.description: Also check on the server (default true)

function.name: %tool.formatSql.name
function.description: Formats SQL text with Chromite's formatter in the dialect of the given or current connection (generic without one); returns sql. Use when the user asks for formatted SQL.

function.name: %tool.getQueryHistory.name
function.description: Statements the user ran in Chromite's query windows (not server statistics), newest first, with time, duration, rows and errors. Use for what the user ran before or to find a statement they mention. For the server's most expensive statements use getTopQueries.

parameter.name: connection
parameter.description: Only this connection (in the chat: the chat's connection)

function.name: %tool.sampleRows.name
function.description: Reads rows of one table or view without writing SQL: optional where and orderBy fragments, limit (default 20) and offset; read-only. Use for a quick look at data. For joins, aggregates or your own SELECT use runSelect; to count rows use countRows.

parameter.name: orderBy
parameter.description: ORDER BY fragment without the keyword, for example created_at DESC

function.name: %tool.countRows.name
function.description: Exact row count of a table or view, optionally with a where condition. Scans the table, so it can be slow on large tables; getTableStatistics gives cheap estimates.

function.name: %tool.profileColumns.name
function.description: Data profile per column: total and non-null rows, distinct values, min, max and the most frequent values. Scans the table once per column (max 30 columns). Use for data quality or value distribution questions. For column types use describeTable.

parameter.name: topN
parameter.description: Most frequent values per column (default 5, 0 for none)

function.name: %tool.compareQueryResults.name
function.description: Runs two read-only SELECTs (same or different connections and databases) and compares the rows by key columns or as whole rows: counts and samples of rows only in A, only in B and different. Use to check that a copy, migration or rewrite returns the same data. To compare plans use comparePlans.

parameter.name: keyColumns
parameter.description: Comma-separated key columns (default: compare whole rows)

function.name: %tool.insertRows.name
function.description: Inserts rows given as JSON objects into a table; values are converted to the column types. WRITE: the user confirms. One call is one transaction on auto-commit connections. For a CSV file use importCsv; for rows of another table copyTable; for INSERT ... SELECT runSql.

function.name: %tool.updateRows.name
function.description: Updates rows identified by key values that cover the primary key or a unique index (other keys are refused), setting the given column values. WRITE: the user confirms. For a set-based UPDATE with a WHERE condition use runSql.

parameter.name: key
parameter.description: JSON object {keyColumn: value} or a JSON array of them

function.name: %tool.deleteRows.name
function.description: Deletes rows identified by key values that cover the primary key or a unique index (other keys are refused). WRITE: the user confirms. For a set-based DELETE with a WHERE condition use runSql.

parameter.name: key
parameter.description: JSON object {keyColumn: value} or a JSON array of them

function.name: %tool.generateDdl.name
function.description: Builds the DDL of a table, view or index change without running it; operation names the matching tool and the other arguments are that tool's. Use it to show the user the exact DDL before calling createTable, alterTable, dropTable, createView, dropView, createIndex or dropIndex. For the DDL of an existing object use getObjectDdl.

parameter.name: columns
parameter.description: createTable: JSON array of {name, type, nullable, default, identity}; createIndex: comma-separated columns with optional ASC/DESC

parameter.name: default
parameter.description: alterTable addColumn: default value or expression

parameter.name: include
parameter.description: createIndex: comma-separated INCLUDE columns (SQL Server, PostgreSQL)

function.name: %tool.createTable.name
function.description: Creates a table from column definitions and an optional primary key. WRITE: the user sees the DDL and confirms. For DDL these arguments cannot express use runSql.

parameter.name: columns
parameter.description: JSON array of {name, type, nullable, default, identity}

function.name: %tool.alterTable.name
function.description: Changes one column of a table: addColumn, dropColumn, renameColumn or alterColumnType. WRITE: the user sees the DDL and confirms. For other ALTER TABLE changes (constraints, table options) use runSql.

function.name: %tool.dropTable.name
function.description: Drops a table with all its data. DANGEROUS: the user confirms. Check getObjectDependencies first. To remove rows only use deleteRows or runSql.

function.name: %tool.createView.name
function.description: Creates a view from a read-only SELECT, or replaces an existing one with replace=true. WRITE: the user sees the DDL and confirms.

function.name: %tool.dropView.name
function.description: Drops a view. DANGEROUS: the user confirms. Check getObjectDependencies first.

function.name: %tool.createIndex.name
function.description: Creates an index on a table: key columns with ASC/DESC, optionally unique and with INCLUDE columns (SQL Server, PostgreSQL). WRITE: the user sees the DDL and confirms. On PostgreSQL try it first with whatIfIndex.

parameter.name: columns
parameter.description: Comma-separated key columns, each optionally ASC or DESC

function.name: %tool.dropIndex.name
function.description: Drops an index of a table. WRITE: the user sees the DDL and confirms. Check getIndexUsage or getUnusedIndexes first.

function.name: %tool.exportData.name
function.description: Writes the rows of a read-only SELECT or of a table to a new CSV, JSON or XLSX file on this computer (default 100,000 rows, max 1,000,000). Use when the user wants a file. To show rows in the chat use runSelect; to back up a database use backupDatabase or dumpDatabase.

parameter.name: file
parameter.description: Absolute path of the file to write on this computer

function.name: %tool.importCsv.name
function.description: Inserts the rows of a CSV file on this computer (header = column names) into an existing table of 'connection'. WRITE: the user confirms. One transaction on auto-commit connections. For rows given in the chat use insertRows.

parameter.name: file
parameter.description: Absolute path of the CSV file

function.name: %tool.copyTable.name
function.description: Copies the rows of a table from sourceConnection (default: the same) into a table of 'connection', optionally creating the target table. WRITE: the user confirms. For large or type-sensitive copies suggest the Data Transfer wizard instead; to check the copy use compareQueryResults.

parameter.name: createTarget
parameter.description: Create the target table from the source columns (default false)

function.name: %tool.listSessions.name
function.description: Server sessions with login, host, program, status, current wait and statement; activeOnly keeps those running something or holding a transaction. Use for who is connected or what is running. For blocking use getBlockingChain; for long statements getLongRunningQueries; for old transactions listOpenTransactions. SQL Server, PostgreSQL, MySQL/MariaDB, Oracle.

parameter.name: activeOnly
parameter.description: Only sessions running something or holding a transaction

function.name: %tool.getBlockingChain.name
function.description: Who blocks whom right now as a tree: head blockers (login, host, program, transaction age, isolation, open transactions, last SQL), waiters (wait type, time, resource, SQL), their locks mapped to objects and indexes, and findings with fix suggestions. Start here for blocking, hanging queries or lock waits. For every lock held use listLocks; for past deadlocks getDeadlocks. SQL Server, PostgreSQL, MySQL/MariaDB, Oracle.

parameter.name: database
parameter.description: Database whose objects the locks are mapped to; default: current

function.name: %tool.listLocks.name
function.description: Held and waited locks grouped by session, object, index and mode, a summary, and lock escalation counters (SQL Server). Use for the full lock picture of a session or object. For who blocks whom start with getBlockingChain. SQL Server, PostgreSQL, MySQL/MariaDB, Oracle.

parameter.name: database
parameter.description: Database whose objects the locks are mapped to

function.name: %tool.getDeadlocks.name
function.description: Deadlocks that already happened: SQL Server system_health deadlock graphs as JSON (victims, processes with SQL and stack, resources with owners and waiters); MySQL/MariaDB the latest InnoDB deadlock; PostgreSQL the counters only; Oracle the ORA-00060 alert log entries with the trace file's deadlock graph. For blocking happening now use getBlockingChain.

function.name: %tool.listOpenTransactions.name
function.description: Server transactions open longer than minSeconds, including idle-in-transaction sessions, with age, locks and last SQL. Use for forgotten transactions that hold locks or log space. For the agent's own transaction use getTransactionStatus. SQL Server, PostgreSQL, MySQL/MariaDB, Oracle.

function.name: %tool.getLongRunningQueries.name
function.description: Statements running now for longer than minSeconds with CPU, reads, waits and blocking. Use for what is slow right now. For statements that were expensive over time use getTopQueries (SQL Server Query Store: getQueryStoreTopQueries). SQL Server, PostgreSQL, MySQL/MariaDB, Oracle.

function.name: %tool.killSession.name
function.description: Ends another server session; its open transaction is rolled back. DANGEROUS and a last resort: only when the user asks, after getBlockingChain or listSessions identified the session; the user confirms and is told when it has an open transaction. To stop the agent's own statement use cancelQuery. SQL Server, PostgreSQL, MySQL/MariaDB, Oracle.

function.name: %tool.getWaitStats.name
function.description: What the server waits on: cumulative wait types since restart without benign ones (SQL Server, MySQL, Oracle) or current session waits (PostgreSQL). Use for a server-wide bottleneck (CPU, I/O, locks, memory). For the waits of blocked sessions use getBlockingChain.

function.name: %tool.getTopQueries.name
function.description: Most expensive statements in the server's cumulative statistics, ordered by cpu, io, duration or executions: SQL Server plan cache, PostgreSQL pg_stat_statements, MySQL performance_schema digests, Oracle V$SQL. Use to find what to tune. For SQL Server history that survives restarts use getQueryStoreTopQueries; for statements running now getLongRunningQueries.

function.name: %tool.getDatabaseSizes.name
function.description: Size of every database on the server (data and log). Use for how big the databases are. For files, free space and largest tables of one database use getSpaceUsage. SQL Server, PostgreSQL, MySQL/MariaDB, Oracle.

function.name: %tool.getSpaceUsage.name
function.description: Space inside one database: data and log files with used and free space, log reuse wait and disk volumes (SQL Server); tablespaces, largest tables and WAL (PostgreSQL); schemas and largest tables (MySQL); tablespace usage (Oracle). Use for full disks or a growing log. For the sizes of all databases use getDatabaseSizes; per table getTableStatistics.

function.name: %tool.getBackupHistory.name
function.description: Backups already taken: last full, differential and log backup per database with age and warnings, and recent backups (SQL Server msdb); WAL archiving (PostgreSQL); RMAN jobs (Oracle); not MySQL. Use for when the last backup ran. To take a backup use backupDatabase (SQL Server) or dumpDatabase (PostgreSQL, MySQL).

function.name: %tool.getJobHistory.name
function.description: Recent runs of the server's scheduler, failures only by default: SQL Server Agent (msdb), PostgreSQL pg_cron, MySQL events, Oracle scheduler. Use for whether any job failed. On SQL Server, for one job's steps and messages use getAgentJobHistory, for job definitions listAgentJobs.

parameter.name: failedOnly
parameter.description: Only failed or canceled runs (default true; getAgentJobHistory defaults to false)

function.name: %tool.getErrorLog.name
function.description: Recent server log entries, optionally only those containing a text: SQL Server error log, PostgreSQL current log file, MySQL 8 error_log table, Oracle alert log. Use for errors, failed logins, crashes or restarts. For deadlock details use getDeadlocks.

parameter.name: contains
parameter.description: Text the entry contains (for example deadlock, error, failed)

function.name: %tool.getServerConfig.name
function.description: Key server and database settings with sanity findings (MAXDOP, cost threshold, memory, auto shrink, shared_buffers, work_mem, autovacuum, buffer pool, ...). Use to review configuration. For version, edition and uptime use getServerInfo. SQL Server, PostgreSQL, MySQL/MariaDB, Oracle.

function.name: %tool.backupDatabase.name
function.description: SQL Server only: BACKUP DATABASE or LOG to a file path on the database server (COPY_ONLY and CHECKSUM by default, so the backup chain is not changed). WRITE: the user sees the T-SQL and confirms. For PostgreSQL or MySQL use dumpDatabase; for past backups getBackupHistory.

parameter.name: file
parameter.description: Backup file path on the database server, not this computer

function.name: %tool.restoreDatabase.name
function.description: SQL Server only: restores a database from a backup file on the database server (the latest full backup set and the sets after it), moving files to the server's default folders. DANGEROUS: the user sees the T-SQL and confirms. For PostgreSQL or MySQL backup files use restoreDump.

parameter.name: file
parameter.description: Backup file path on the database server, not this computer

function.name: %tool.dumpDatabase.name
function.description: PostgreSQL (pg_dump) and MySQL/MariaDB (mysqldump) only: backs up a database, or some schemas (PostgreSQL) or tables (MySQL), to a new file on the computer where Chromite runs, with the client tools of the connection's Local Client setting. Never overwrites a file. WRITE: the user sees the command line and confirms. Long runs report progress. For SQL Server use backupDatabase; to export query rows use exportData.

parameter.name: file
parameter.description: Absolute path of the new backup file (a folder for format=directory) on this computer; it must not exist, its folder must

parameter.name: format
parameter.description: PostgreSQL output format (default custom; plain is a SQL script). MySQL always writes a SQL script

parameter.name: schemas
parameter.description: PostgreSQL: comma-separated schemas to back up (default: the whole database)

parameter.name: tables
parameter.description: MySQL: comma-separated tables to back up (default: the whole database)

parameter.name: inserts
parameter.description: PostgreSQL: INSERT commands instead of COPY (default false)

parameter.name: clean
parameter.description: PostgreSQL: add DROP commands before the CREATE commands (default false)

parameter.name: create
parameter.description: PostgreSQL: add a CREATE DATABASE command (default false)

parameter.name: routines
parameter.description: MySQL: include procedures and functions (default true)

function.name: %tool.restoreDump.name
function.description: PostgreSQL (pg_restore, or psql for a plain SQL script) and MySQL/MariaDB (mysql) only: restores a backup file on the computer where Chromite runs into an existing database, with the client tools of the connection's Local Client setting; the PostgreSQL format is detected from the file. DANGEROUS: the user sees the command line and confirms. For SQL Server use restoreDatabase.

parameter.name: file
parameter.description: Absolute path of the backup file (or directory-format folder) on this computer

parameter.name: format
parameter.description: PostgreSQL: the backup's format (default: detected from the file)

parameter.name: clean
parameter.description: PostgreSQL pg_restore: drop objects before recreating them (default false)

parameter.name: noOwner
parameter.description: PostgreSQL pg_restore: do not restore ownership (default false)

parameter.name: stopOnError
parameter.description: PostgreSQL: stop at the first error (psql ON_ERROR_STOP, pg_restore --exit-on-error; default false)

parameter.name: disableForeignKeyChecks
parameter.description: MySQL: disable foreign key checks while restoring (default false)

function.name: %tool.listAgentJobs.name
function.description: SQL Server Agent: the agent service state and the jobs with enabled flag, current status and step, last run outcome and time, next run, category, owner. Use for which jobs exist or are running. For one job's steps and schedules use getAgentJob; for run history getAgentJobHistory; for failures of all jobs getJobHistory.

parameter.name: filter
parameter.description: Optional text to match in the job name or category

function.name: %tool.getAgentJob.name
function.description: SQL Server Agent: one job's definition: steps (subsystem, database, command, on success/failure actions, retries) and schedules (description, next run), plus its current state. Use to explain a job or before starting or stopping it.

function.name: %tool.getAgentJobHistory.name
function.description: SQL Server Agent: run history, newest first: each run's outcome (step 0) and its steps with status, duration, retries and the server message; one job or all jobs. Use for why a job failed. For a quick failure list of all jobs use getJobHistory.

parameter.name: job
parameter.description: Job name or job_id; empty for all jobs

parameter.name: failedOnly
parameter.description: Only runs and steps that failed or were canceled (default false)

function.name: %tool.startAgentJob.name
function.description: SQL Server Agent: starts a job now (msdb.dbo.sp_start_job), optionally at a step. The job runs asynchronously; follow it with listAgentJobs and getAgentJobHistory. WRITE: the user sees the T-SQL and confirms.

parameter.name: step
parameter.description: Step name to start at (default: the job's start step)

function.name: %tool.stopAgentJob.name
function.description: SQL Server Agent: stops a running job (msdb.dbo.sp_stop_job). WRITE: the user sees the T-SQL and confirms.

function.name: %tool.setAgentJobEnabled.name
function.description: SQL Server Agent: enables or disables a job (msdb.dbo.sp_update_job @enabled). A disabled job does not run on its schedules but can still be started by hand. WRITE: the user sees the T-SQL and confirms.

parameter.name: enabled
parameter.description: true to enable, false to disable

function.name: %tool.getTableStatistics.name
function.description: Per table (one table or a schema): row count, table and index sizes, statistics last update, rows sampled, modifications since the update, dead rows and vacuum/analyze times. Use for stale statistics, table growth or cheap row counts of many tables. For an exact count use countRows. SQL Server, PostgreSQL, MySQL/MariaDB, Oracle.

function.name: %tool.getIndexUsage.name
function.description: How existing indexes were used since the server started: seeks, scans, lookups, updates, key and included columns, lock escalations; one table or a schema. Use to judge whether indexes pay off. For only unused or duplicate indexes use getUnusedIndexes; for index definitions listIndexes. SQL Server, PostgreSQL, MySQL (performance_schema), Oracle (statistics only).

function.name: %tool.getMissingIndexes.name
function.description: Indexes that may be missing in a database: SQL Server optimizer suggestions with a CREATE INDEX; PostgreSQL large tables read mostly by sequential scans; Oracle full scans of large tables in cached plans with the filter predicates an index could serve; not MySQL. Use for database-wide index suggestions. For one query use explainQuery.

function.name: %tool.getUnusedIndexes.name
function.description: Indexes that are written but never read since the last restart, and duplicate or left-prefix indexes, in a database or schema. Use before dropping indexes. SQL Server, PostgreSQL, MySQL/MariaDB, Oracle (index usage tracking DBA_INDEX_USAGE, 12.2+).

function.name: %tool.getIndexFragmentation.name
function.description: Fragmentation with REBUILD/REORGANIZE suggestions (SQL Server), dead rows and leaf density (PostgreSQL, pgstattuple if installed), reclaimable space (MySQL); one table or a schema; not Oracle. Use for index maintenance questions.

function.name: %tool.getRoutineStats.name
function.description: Run-time statistics of one procedure, function or trigger and of each statement inside it with its start line (SQL Server, Oracle V$SQL PROGRAM_LINE#); function statistics and nested statements (PostgreSQL); program statistics (MySQL). Use to find the slow statement inside a routine, then getRoutineSource for its code and getCachedPlans (SQL Server) for its plans.

parameter.name: name
parameter.description: Procedure, function or trigger: name or schema.name

function.name: %tool.getCachedPlans.name
function.description: SQL Server only: plans in the plan cache for each statement of a routine (by start line) or of statements containing a text, parsed like explainQuery (operators, warnings, compiled parameter values). Use to see the plan the server actually uses, for example for parameter sniffing. For a fresh estimate use explainQuery.

function.name: %tool.getQueryStoreTopQueries.name
function.description: SQL Server Query Store of a database: the most expensive queries of the last hours (CPU, duration, logical reads, executions) with their plan count. Unlike getTopQueries it survives restarts and plan cache eviction. Says clearly when Query Store is off.

function.name: %tool.getQueryStoreRegressions.name
function.description: SQL Server Query Store of a database: queries whose average duration in the recent window is worse than in the earlier window, with the plan ids of both windows (plan_changed = a different plan is the likely cause). Use when a query got slower than before. Says clearly when Query Store is off.

parameter.name: historyMinutes
parameter.description: Earlier window in minutes before the recent one (default 10080 = 7 days)

function.name: %tool.getQueryStoreForcedPlans.name
function.description: SQL Server Query Store of a database: plans forced on queries (manually or by automatic tuning) with their force failure count and last failure reason. Read only: it does not force or unforce. Says clearly when Query Store is off.

function.name: %tool.whatIfIndex.name
function.description: PostgreSQL with the hypopg extension: estimated plan of a statement before and after a hypothetical index (nothing is built; it exists only in the agent's session for this call) and the plan comparison. Use before proposing createIndex on PostgreSQL. Without hypopg in the database it answers available=false with the reason.

parameter.name: index
parameter.description: CREATE INDEX statement of the hypothetical index

function.name: %tool.listLibraryQueries.name
function.description: Saved queries of the user's Chromite Query Library: id, name, description, folder, target connection, parameters, thresholds. Use when the user mentions a saved, library or monitoring query. For statements the user ran recently use getQueryHistory.

parameter.name: contains
parameter.description: Text in name, description or SQL

function.name: %tool.getLibraryQuery.name
function.description: One Query Library entry with its SQL, parameters and thresholds. Use to explain a saved query or to learn its parameters before runLibraryQuery.

function.name: %tool.runLibraryQuery.name
function.description: Runs one Query Library query with parameters (bound, not concatenated) on its target or the given connection and judges the result against its thresholds. Queries that may change data become WRITE and need 'connection'. For all checks of a folder use runMonitoringChecks.

function.name: %tool.runMonitoringChecks.name
function.description: Runs every read-only query of a Query Library folder and judges each against its @threshold entries: OK, WARN, CRITICAL, NO_THRESHOLDS, SKIPPED, ERROR, plus a summary. Use for system status from the user's own monitoring queries; without such a folder use the health tools (listSessions, getBlockingChain, getWaitStats, ...).

function.name: %tool.openInEditor.name
function.shortDescription: Opens SQL in a new query window for the user; does not run it.
function.description: Opens SQL in a new query window of the Chromite app for the user; does not run it. Use when the user wants the SQL in an editor. To change the text of an open window use editQueryWindow.

function.name: %tool.listQueryWindows.name
function.description: Lists the query windows open in the Chromite app: id, title, connection, database, saved file, unsaved changes, active window, running query, text length, caret and selection. Use to find the window the user means.

function.name: %tool.getQueryWindowText.name
function.shortDescription: Reads the SQL of the user's query window: all, the selection or the statement at the caret.
function.description: Reads the text of an open query window (default: the active one): the whole text, the selection, or the SQL statement at the caret, with its offsets. Use when the user refers to this query, the editor or the selected SQL.

parameter.name: window
parameter.description: Window id from listQueryWindows (default: the active window)
parameter.shortDescription: Window id; default: the active window

parameter.name: part
parameter.description: all (default), selection, or statement (the SQL statement at the caret)

function.name: %tool.editQueryWindow.name
function.description: Changes the text of an open query window (default: the active one): insert at the caret, replace the selection, or replace the whole text. Never runs or saves the text; the user confirms a preview of the change and can undo it with one Ctrl+Z. To open SQL in a new window use openInEditor.

parameter.name: window
parameter.description: Window id from listQueryWindows (default: the active window)

parameter.name: mode
parameter.description: insert (at the caret), replaceSelection or replaceAll

parameter.name: text
parameter.description: New text (empty with replaceSelection deletes the selection)
